label: Rates confirmed for April 2027
title: National Living Wage rises to £13.21 from April 2027: what employers should do now
summary: The minimum wage goes up for every age group on 1 April 2027. Here are the new rates and the payroll checks worth doing before then.
body:
GOV.UK now shows the minimum wage rates that will apply from April 2027. Rates change on 1 April every year, and every employer needs to update pay for staff on or near the minimum.

The new rates

  • Age 21 and over (National Living Wage): £13.21 an hour, up from £12.71
  • Age 18 to 20: £11.27, up from £10.85
  • Under 18: £8.31, up from £8
  • Apprentices: £8.31, up from £8

The apprentice rate applies to apprentices under 19, or 19 and over in the first year of their apprenticeship. After that, they are entitled to the rate for their age.

What it costs

For a worker aged 21 or over on 40 hours a week, 50p more an hour is about £1,040 a year, before employer National Insurance and pension contributions.

What I would do

  • Update pay rates from the first pay period that starts on or after 1 April 2027.
  • Watch birthdays. The rate depends on the worker's age at the start of each pay period, so staff moving into a new age band get the higher rate from the first pay period that starts after their birthday.
  • Check deductions. Uniform costs, unpaid training time and time spent on tasks before or after a shift can take pay below the minimum even when the hourly rate looks right.
  • Budget now. Put the increase into your 2027 forecast, including the knock-on effect on supervisors' pay.
